Subject: High latency & 502 spike — MerchantX (prod)

Hi Rohan —

We started seeing a large jump in end-to-end latency for MerchantX checkout calls around 07:30 PST. 95th latency is up to 1.8s (normally ~220ms) and we're seeing a burst of 502s that map to requests routed to us-east-1/az1. This is impacting ~8% of checkout traffic and is causing customer dropoff.

Our ops team pulled logs and attached the top-level traces and a p95 plot. Can you confirm whether Redwood rerouted traffic or if there's a regional degradation? We need a short-lived geo rehome to us-west-2 while you investigate — we cannot sustain this hit for the Black Friday pre-sell.

Please advise ASAP.

—Asha

Quick engineering readout (initial):

- Symptom: latency p95 jump and 502s concentrated on us-east-1 AZ 'az1' across model-serving nodes. Error traces show 502s from the runtime layer when attempting to access KV cache segments; timeouts then cascade.
- Probable cause: KV-cache segment eviction + kernel-level throttling on a subset of GPU hosts in az1. Metrics show a KV-cache miss amplification at 07:27 and a spike in host I/O wait.
- Immediate mitigations: 1) soft-evacuate traffic off az1 to us-east-1/az3 and us-west-2; 2) increase cache TTL and reduce batch sizes for MerchantX routes to lower host pressure; 3) schedule host remediation (reboot/drain) in parallel.

I'm preparing a play-by-play; requesting authorization for cross-region steer now. If we get the go-ahead from Marissa/exec, ops will enact the geo rehome (target 30–45s propagation for our edge routing rules).

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Asha — quick post-mitigation update and action items: we completed the soft geo rehome at 09:22 PST on Nov 20 (traffic shifted: ~92% -> us-west-2, 8% to us-east-1/az3 for monitoring). Observed effects: p95 latency dropped from 1.8s -> 260ms within three minutes; 502s fell to baseline.

Current status:
- Root cause (working hypothesis): KV-cache segment eviction due to a combination of model-prefetch bursts and host kernel scheduling oddities on a small subset of az1 hosts.
- Next steps (engineering): Olga + Hannah to drain and reprovision affected hosts in az1, increase KV-cache segment headroom for MerchantX, and apply an emergency batching throttle to the MerchantX route for 24 hours.
- Commercials: Marissa has approved a temporary credit offer; I'll draft the note. If MerchantX wants a permanent Dedicated pool to avoid cross-AZ interference, we can scope that (Vivek — can you prepare a cost delta + lead time).
